task.description: Focused security re-gate on what changed since my original PASS (step-03b): (1) index/constraint NAME restoration via ALTER INDEX RENAME (design section 0.6, mechanism step 3.5, INV-7), fixing Ecto's name-based unique_constraint/3 error mapping; (2) atomic template build via a randomized staging schema + ALTER SCHEMA RENAME TO 'tenant_template' as the commit point (design section 0.7, INV-8), fixing a crash-safety defect where a failed build left a permanently wedged empty template. Judge: (a) whether index/constraint renaming disturbs the audit_entries/repository_artifacts immutability guarantee I previously verified; (b) whether the staging schema introduces a new hazard -- mistakable-for-a-tenant, reachable by the reaper, cleaned up on build failure or accumulating as debris, and a rename-collision window between concurrent builders; (c) re-confirm tenant isolation (FK/sequence/trigger-function/column-type independence, survival of template drop) on the current code; (d) whether the two new changes touch a tenant-data path differently, and whether INV-7/INV-8 as named in the design are real invariants or just wishes. Do not re-litigate what was already passed and unchanged.

result.summary:
Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0427-20260904/step-06-code-designer-index-names.json and step-07-elixir-dev-index-names.json in full, then read the current test/support/tenant_template.ex directly (not diffed piecemeal against memory of the prior version) to see both new mechanisms as they actually exist on disk. git diff main...HEAD -- test/support/tenant_fixture.ex confirmed unchanged since my original review (44 insertions/8 deletions, identical stat to step-03b's own record) -- consistent with ELIXIR-DEV's own claim that this file needed no further change. git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/ still shows zero code files (only the design doc), so the scope-test override from my original PASS (tenant schema isolation is the evidence-producing mechanism several invariants rest on, regardless of which directory the code lives in) applies identically here -- re-applied, not re-litigated.

(a) THE RENAME AND THE IMMUTABILITY GUARANTEE -- re-verified end-to-end on a probe reproducing the CURRENT code's mechanism, including index rename, not the version I reviewed originally. Built probe_tpl/probe_clone in letflow_dev with a users-shaped case (a serial PK, a named UNIQUE table constraint, a partial/expression unique index, an FK, and the two-trigger/one-function immutability shape), ran the clone sequence in the CURRENT code's exact order (LIKE loop, THEN index rename via schema-qualifier-normalized structural pairing matching structural_indexdef/1 + normalize/2, THEN FK re-add, THEN sequence recreation, THEN trigger/function re-add), confirmed: the auto-generated clone index names (parents_val_key, parents_lower_idx) were correctly renamed to the template's own names (parents_val_uq, parents_val_idx) via ALTER INDEX RENAME, and the owning pg_constraint row's conname changed ATOMICALLY with the index rename (queried pg_constraint directly after rename: conname=parents_val_uq, contype=u -- exactly ELIXIR-DEV's own claim, independently reproduced, not inherited). A duplicate INSERT after the full mechanism (index rename + FK + sequence + trigger steps) raised 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "parents_val_uq"' -- the TEMPLATE's own name, confirming the Ecto-relevant string match this fix exists to restore. Then, on the SAME clone, post-full-mechanism: UPDATE against the clone -> 'ERROR: audit is immutable' (rejected); DELETE -> identically rejected. Dropped the template schema entirely (DROP SCHEMA probe_tpl CASCADE); UPDATE against the SAME clone row post-drop -> 'ERROR: audit is immutable' again, byte-identical to pre-drop. FK still enforced post-drop (insert with nonexistent clone-local parent -> rejected with real FK violation). Sequence still clone-local and functional post-drop (new row got a real, correctly-allocated id). VERDICT: index/constraint renaming does NOT disturb the immutability guarantee in any way -- it operates on a structurally disjoint catalog surface (pg_class/pg_index naming) from the trigger/function re-add (pg_trigger/pg_proc), runs at a different, non-overlapping mechanism step (step 3.5, strictly before step 6), and my own reproduction of the CURRENT combined sequence confirms both guarantees hold simultaneously and independently. This is a genuine re-verification against the current mechanism, not a re-assertion of the prior probe's result -- the two probes are structurally different runs on different code paths that happen to reach the same, correct outcome.

(b) THE STAGING SCHEMA -- this is where I spent the most scrutiny, per the coordinator's own framing, and I FOUND A REAL, undesigned exposure the design itself already names but does not close (see the filed issue below) -- not severe enough to FAIL this gate, but not something to wave through as harmless either.

Mistaken-for-a-tenant: NO, confirmed independently, not inherited. generate_staging_schema_name/0 (tenant_template.ex:314-317) produces "tenant_template_build_" <> 32 lowercase hex chars via :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(16) |> Base.encode16(case: :lower). I verified with bash regex against a real generated example (tenant_template_build_3777820c86e833c9d46fd7956f4b0e21): it does NOT match tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's pattern (schema_name.ex:195-206 requires 'tenant_' <> EXACTLY 32 lowercase hex chars with nothing else -- the staging name's suffix after 'tenant_' is 'template_build_<32hex>', 47 chars, containing non-hex letters t/m/p/l/d, fails both the length and the character-class checks), and does NOT match TenantSchemaReaper's own @schema_name_format (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:127, ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ -- same reasoning). Confirmed by reading both regexes directly, not by trusting the design's own claim. The three grounds I established in my original PASS for why 'tenant_template' cannot be mistaken for a tenant (schema_name_for_tenant/1 cannot produce it, tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 cannot resolve it, no Registration row is ever inserted for it) hold in the SAME shape for the staging name: it is never producible by schema_name_for_tenant/1 (which only ever emits 'tenant_' <> 32-hex), never resolvable by tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (confirmed above), and the throwaway Registration row insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1 targets the staging name value (not a hardcoded literal) via the SAME Repo.insert_all/3 bypass-of-validate_format mechanism I verified originally, deleted before build_template!/0 proceeds past the migration step -- confirmed by reading lines 268-310 directly. INV-1: APPLIES, PASS on this axis.

Reaper reach: NO, confirmed independently. TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2's candidate query (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:169) is 'SELECT id, tenant_id, schema_name FROM tenant_schemas WHERE provisioned_at < $1' -- it selects candidates from the tenant_schemas/Registration table only, never by walking pg_namespace. Since the staging schema's own throwaway Registration row is deleted before the schema is renamed (and even while it exists transiently, its schema_name value is the staging name, which fails @schema_name_format at test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:176's own Regex.match? guard before reclaim_row/2 is ever called -- confirmed by reading that guard directly, not assumed), the reaper is structurally incapable of selecting a staging schema for reclamation, for the identical reason it cannot reach the final 'tenant_template' name. Grepped for any OTHER code path enumerating pg_namespace or information_schema.schemata by pattern (test/support/*.ex, lib/letflow/*.ex) -- the only hits are tenant_fixture.ex's assert_schema_complete!/2, which checks ONE specific, parameter-bound schema name it already knows, never an enumeration/pattern scan. No code path exists today that could stumble onto a staging schema by accident.

Cleanup on build failure -- THIS IS THE REAL FINDING, confirmed by reading the code directly rather than trusting the design's own framing of it as merely 'inert debris.' build_template!/0 (lines 268-310) has NO rescue/after block of its own around the staging schema's lifecycle -- CREATE SCHEMA (step 1) commits immediately and unconditionally; if replay_migrations/2 fails, or if template_self_check!/1 raises (the exact failure mode INV-8 exists to make loud), the exception propagates up through ensure_template!/0's own try/after, which releases ONLY the advisory lock (line 122-124) -- it does not DROP the staging schema. The randomly-named staging schema is left behind as a real, orphaned Postgres object every time a build fails after CREATE SCHEMA but before the final ALTER SCHEMA RENAME. I confirmed this by reading the full function body top to bottom and finding no DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS <staging> cleanup path anywhere on the failure route -- this is not a hypothetical reading, it is what the code as written does. The design's own OQ-7 (section 9, lines 2108-2133) states this EXACTLY and explicitly, unprompted by this re-gate: 'leaves a randomly-named, orphaned staging schema... behind whenever a build attempt fails,' names it 'harmless, inert debris,' and explicitly declines to add a sweep for it, reasoning that a test-run's database is ephemeral between full-suite invocations via mix ecto.reset -- but ALSO explicitly acknowledges 'a long-lived dev database that is NOT reset between many interrupted local mix test runs... could accumulate several,' citing the EXACT debris class ISSUE-FIXER's step-05 handoff and ORCH's own earlier probing already produced ONCE on this very run. The coordinator's own framing ('this run was already badly hurt by exactly that class of leftover state') is not a hypothetical concern raised by this re-gate -- it is a documented, self-acknowledged, currently-open design gap (OQ-7), not a newly-discovered defect. My independent verification confirms the design's own account is accurate (no code-level cleanup exists) rather than aspirational. Severity judgement: this is a MAJOR process-hygiene/operational-risk finding, NOT a security BLOCKER. It is not a security exposure under any of INV-1 through INV-9 because: the debris is provably inert (cannot be mistaken for or resolve as a tenant, cannot be reached by the reaper, carries no Registration/tenant_schemas row, holds no real tenant data -- it is a copy of empty/near-empty tenant-shaped tables from a failed or partial migration replay, structurally identical in risk shape to the ALREADY-ACCEPTED SandboxPool crashed-schema debris class the design cites as precedent) -- but it IS a real resource-accumulation and eventual-collision-surface risk in a long-lived local dev database (enough accumulated staging schemas could, in principle, eventually exhaust something, though nothing tenant-data-relevant), and it is exactly the failure MODE that already cost this run real time and required ORCH's own multi-step diagnosis earlier in this same run. Filed as an issue below rather than blocking on it, because OQ-7 already names it as a known, tracked-in-the-design gap rather than a silently-shipped one, and because the design's own reasoning for why it is inert (not a security hazard) independently checks out.

Rename-collision window between concurrent builders -- NO NEW RACE, confirmed by reading ensure_template!/0's control flow directly. The session-level pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock pair (lines 97, 122-124) still wraps the ENTIRE unless template_built_in_db?() do ... build_template!() ... end sequence, unchanged in scope from what I reviewed originally -- it is not narrowed to just the rename step, it covers staging-schema creation, migration, self-check, AND the final rename as one serialized unit per BEAM VM. Two concurrent callers within one partition's connection pool cannot both reach build_template!/0 unboxed simultaneously; the second waits on the advisory lock, then re-checks template_built_in_db?() (line 102) and finds the template already exists, skipping a redundant build entirely. Independently, even absent the lock, two concurrent staging builds could not collide with EACH OTHER on CREATE SCHEMA, since generate_staging_schema_name/0 draws 128 bits of randomness (:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(16)) per attempt -- collision probability is cryptographically negligible, not merely 'unlikely.' No rename-collision window exists.

(c) TENANT ISOLATION -- re-confirmed on the current code via the same combined probe as (a): FK re-add (readd_foreign_keys!/1, unchanged from my original review) still rewrites the UNQUOTED template qualifier to the clone's own qualifier: confirmed the clone's FK constraint definition read back as 'REFERENCES probe_clone.parents(id)', not template-qualified, both before and after the template was dropped. Sequence recreation (recreate_sequences!/1, unchanged) still produces a clone-local sequence surviving template drop: confirmed a post-drop INSERT allocated a correct, clone-local id. Trigger/function re-add (readd_triggers_and_functions!/1, unchanged) still produces a distinct, clone-owned function object whose guarantee survives template drop, per (a) above. Column-type/collation independence (dimension #13's underlying concern) is unaffected by this rework -- no migration in priv/repo/migrations/ introduces a custom DOMAIN/ENUM/COLLATION today (re-confirmed dormant, same grep as my original review, unchanged since then), and neither of the two new mechanisms (index rename, staging-schema build) touches column type or collation objects at all -- index rename operates on pg_class/pg_index, the staging-schema mechanism only changes WHICH schema name the existing, unmodified build sequence targets. INV-1: APPLIES, PASS, re-confirmed on current code rather than merely re-asserted from the prior review.

(d) DOES ANYTHING TOUCH A TENANT-DATA PATH DIFFERENTLY -- NO. Both new mechanisms are still entirely within test/support/, confirmed via git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/ showing zero code changes (the design doc is the only lib/ diff, exactly as before). Neither mechanism adds a new call into lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex beyond what was already reviewed (replay_migrations/2, schema_name_for_tenant/1, both called exactly as before, only the schema_name argument's VALUE differs per build attempt now). INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES, PASS -- this handoff plus my original step-03b handoff together constitute that proof for the full current mechanism.

INV-7/INV-8 AS NAMED IN THE DESIGN -- flagged explicitly per the dispatch's own question, because this naming is a real hazard to a future reader, not merely a style note. The design's INV-7 ('index/constraint NAME parity is what makes Ecto's error-mapping layer resolve a Postgres constraint violation back to a changeset field by matching that name') and INV-8 ('the literal name tenant_template never exists in a half-built state') are BOTH real, checkable, currently-true properties of this specific mechanism -- not wishes. INV-7 is enforced by an actual runtime assertion (parity dimension #4(b), check_index_names/2, independently confirmed present and structurally correct via my own probe reproducing its logic) that runs every suite invocation per the design's own INV-5. INV-8 is enforced by the atomic rename-as-commit-point structure itself, which I independently verified holds (build_template!/0 has no other path to make 'tenant_template' exist except the final ALTER SCHEMA RENAME, confirmed by reading the function's control flow). BUT: these are NOT the same INV-1..INV-9 namespace as docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md, which SECURITY-REVIEWER gates against -- security-invariants.md's own INV-9 is SSRF/outbound-URL validation (REQ-204), a completely different, already-shipped invariant. The design doc's 'INV-7'/'INV-8' are LOCAL, doc-scoped invariant labels for THIS design's own internal properties (correctness/crash-safety of the clone mechanism), not entries in the canonical security-invariants.md numbered list, and must never be cited as if they were -- a future reader skimming for 'INV-8' in a security context could otherwise conflate this design-local label with a security-invariants.md entry that does not exist at that number. Recording this distinction explicitly, as the dispatch asked, rather than silently treating them as equivalent to the canonical list. They are real invariants FOR THIS DESIGN'S OWN CORRECTNESS, independently verified true above -- but they are not SECURITY-REVIEWER gate invariants and should not be renumbered into or confused with security-invariants.md's own list.

INVARIANT SUMMARY (canonical security-invariants.md list, re-run against the DELTA only, not restated in full from step-03b): INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES, PASS, re-verified on current code including the new index-rename step, which does not disturb it. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged (S4/S5 not started). INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES, PASS -- grepped the current file, no secret material introduced by either new mechanism (index/constraint names and a randomized hex staging-schema name are not secrets). INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES, PASS -- this handoff is that proof for the delta. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation, canonical list): APPLIES, PASS -- the new rename_indexes_to_template_names!/2 and index_name_defs_by_table/1 functions use bind parameters ($1) for the schema_name filter in their discovery query and interpolate only catalog-derived identifiers (clone_name, template_name, table names) into the ALTER INDEX DDL via ~s(...) -- the same already-accepted pattern (Postgres-catalog-sourced names, never caller/test-input-controlled strings) my original review verified for the FK/trigger mechanisms; generate_staging_schema_name/0's output is likewise never interpolated FROM external input, it is generated internally by :crypto.strong_rand_bytes. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths, canonical list): APPLIES, PASS with the MINOR/MAJOR note above about staging-schema cleanup -- the lack of a rescue-and-drop around build_template!/0 is a resource-cleanup gap, not an unhandled-crash-into-shared-state hazard (the function still raises correctly, per its own contract, and test/support/ code never runs inside a shared production process where a crash could affect another tenant's in-flight work). INV-9 (SSRF): NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged.

No FAIL on any applicable invariant. The staging-schema debris gap is real, self-acknowledged by the design (OQ-7), independently confirmed present in the code, and not a security hazard under any canonical invariant -- filed as an issue rather than gated on, consistent with 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and the coordinator's own instruction to FAIL only if a genuine hazard exists.

issues.description: Staging-schema debris (tenant_template_build_<32hex>) is left behind, unswept, whenever a template build fails after CREATE SCHEMA but before the final ALTER SCHEMA RENAME TO 'tenant_template' -- confirmed by reading build_template!/0 (test/support/tenant_template.ex:268-310) directly: no rescue/after block drops the staging schema on failure, and ensure_template!/0's own try/after (lines 99-124) only releases the advisory lock, not the staging schema. The design's own OQ-7 (lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md, section 9) names this exact gap, calls it inert-but-real debris, and explicitly leaves TenantSchemaReaper without a corresponding sweep pattern for it, reasoning that per-invocation database resets bound the damage -- but also explicitly acknowledges a long-lived, non-reset local dev database could accumulate several, citing the SAME debris class that already cost this run real diagnostic time earlier (ORCH's own step-05-adjacent probing). Confirmed structurally inert and not a security hazard (cannot be mistaken for a tenant or the live template under any of the three grounds already established for 'tenant_template' itself; cannot be reached by TenantSchemaReaper's tenant_schemas-table-driven query; carries no Registration row past the throwaway-row's own deletion). Recommend: either (a) wrap build_template!/0's body in a rescue that issues DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS <staging> CASCADE before re-raising, closing the gap directly and cheaply (a single extra DDL statement only on the failure path, zero cost on the success path), or (b) give TenantSchemaReaper a second sweep pattern for tenant_template_build_* schemas keyed on age via pg_namespace/creation-time inference, per OQ-7's own proposed shape. Not a gate condition for this run -- OQ-7 already tracks it as a known, open design question, not a silently-shipped gap -- but should not remain open indefinitely given this run's own history with exactly this debris class.

result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER for re-confirmation of the delta (idiom, supervision integrity, scope creep) if not already re-gated; otherwise proceed to merge. Recommend ORCH file the staging-schema-cleanup MAJOR (OQ-7 closure) as a tracked follow-up issue via the standard ISSUE_QUEUE.md path rather than leaving it open-ended in the design doc alone.
